case_title: Surender Kaushik v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_occupation: Secretary of the Sanjeev Memorial Education Society (appellant No. 1); no other occupation stated
accused_victim_relationship: Co-members of the same society (the complainant in FIR No. 442 and several accused sat on the society's governing body); alleged dispute over society property
evidence_type: Not stated (no trial; only FIR-stage allegations and affidavits referred to)
high_court_outcome: Writ petition (Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 15077 of 2012) rejected insofar as it declined to quash FIR No. 442 of 2012; directions on surrender and interim bail issued; validity of second FIR not dealt with
neutral_facts: A complaint by one member of a society running educational institutions alleged that several persons, acting in collusion with another individual, had prepared fake and fraudulent documents. It was alleged that the signatures of members had been forged to show their participation in general and executive meetings that those members had not attended. A separate application alleged that the accused had fabricated an affidavit bearing forged signatures and filed it before a Deputy Registrar of the society registry. On the basis of that application, a further first information report was registered for offences of cheating, forgery, criminal breach of trust and criminal intimidation. A later complaint by another member of the governing body alleged that twelve persons had conspired to prepare forged documents recording meetings held on different dates, had fabricated the signatures of members, and had filed those papers before the competent authority. The complaint alleged that the purpose was to take the society's property and funds. Members had filed affidavits stating that they had never taken part in the meetings or signed the papers. The investigation proceeded on the basis of these complaints, the application and the affidavits, which formed the material available on the allegations.
number_of_offences: 7 alleged in FIR No. 442 of 2012; 0 finally upheld (no conviction before the Supreme Court)
financial_property_loss: Not stated (alleged intent to grab society property and funds; no amount given)
premeditation_planning: Not stated by the Court; the complaint alleged a conspiracy among the accused
motive: alleged: grabbing the property and funds of the society
key_evidence_accepted: None assessed; the Court relied on the distinct spectrum and separate allegations in the two FIRs
bail_history: High Court issued directions for surrender before the concerned court and grant of interim bail; the Supreme Court did not examine these directions
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR No. 442 registered 4.9.2012); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 12.10.2012; Supreme Court: 14.02.2013
legal_representation: Appellants: Mr. Nagendra Rai, senior counsel; State: Mr. R.K. Dash, senior counsel; fourth respondent (complainant): Mr. Altaf Ahmed, senior counsel
investigation_status: FIR No. 274/2012 registered (ss.420, 467, 468, 471 IPC); FIR No. 425/2012 registered 21.8.2012 on Magistrate's direction; FIR No. 442/2012 (Crime No. 491/2012) registered 4.9.2012 on Magistrate's order; no charge sheet mentioned
appeal_history: Trial court: none (FIR stage); High Court: declined to quash FIR No. 442 of 2012 (12.10.2012); Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: State (Mr. R.K. Dash) argued no absolute bar on a second FIR where allegations come from a different spectrum, different versions and different accused, and that the cited decisions are distinguishable; the complainant's counsel (Mr. Altaf Ahmed) argued distinct offences, overlapping features, and that investigation should not be scuttled
defence_argument: Appellants (Mr. Nagendra Rai) argued the second FIR for the same cognizable offence was barred by law, so that under Bhajan Lal the FIR should be quashed; relied on T.T. Antony, Pandurang Chandrakant Mhatre and Babubhai
legal_principle_applied: Lodging two FIRs for the same incident is not permissible, but the sameness rule is restricted: it does not bar a counter FIR or rival versions; the bar is on further complaints by the same complainant against the same accused after registration, causing improvement of facts
precedent_relied_upon: Upkar Singh v. Ved Prakash (2004) 13 SCC 292 (relied on); also referred to: T.T. Antony (2001) 6 SCC 181; Babubhai v. State of Gujarat (2010) 12 SCC 254; Ram Lal Narang (1979) 2 SCC 322; Kari Choudhary (2002) 1 SCC 714; State of Bihar v. J.A.C. Saldanha (1980) 1 SCC 554; State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992 Supp (1) SCC 335)
other_sentence_order: None beyond dismissal; the Court left the commencement and conclusion of trial to the concerned court and noted the parties may seek a single trial court
